thesis: v1 has one move: the cursor comes near and letters get wider. After ten seconds there is nothing left to find, and nothing keeps moving once the cursor stops. v2 keeps the Swiss spec-sheet DNA (paper, ink, IKB, Anybody/Archivo/Plex Mono, fitted lines, grain) and turns the page into a lab sheet. Each big moment is a real simulation with its own action. Each one is drawn only with print techniques and labelled live in mono, like a figure in a paper. FIG.1: the name is a plucked string. A damped 1D wave chain drives wdth/wght, so a flick sends a crest through 4BOOSER that bounces off both ends while the line stays exactly full width, and live axis readouts sit under every letter. FIG.2: Klein pigment. A stable-fluids simulation whose density is printed as a crisp screen-print edge that dries into halftone. It shows through a difference layer whose colour is chosen so that paper prints as IKB #002FA7 and ink prints as gold #D8AA2C (Klein's IKB and Monogold), and the stain scrolls with the page. FIG.3: the footer phrase is 22 rigid bodies held on springs at their typeset positions. Hit them and they break loose, pile up and get bolder with each impact, until '(Re-set type)' springs them home. The work index drops the stock hover card for two riso plates that slip out of register and shear in time (slit-scan), and project titles physically lift into the case sheet. Rules: every effect needs a print metaphor, every effect settles back to a readable page within seconds, and there are three physics actions (pluck, paint, throw) instead of one. Moves below are ranked by wow-per-risk. If time is short, build in this order: FIG.1, FIG.2, FIG.3, then work.
v1_weaknesses: One interaction everywhere. The hero, the footer lines and the services numerals all do 'nearby → wider/heavier'. Nothing has momentum: letters snap back the moment the cursor leaves, nothing travels or bounces, and there is nothing new to find after about 10 seconds.
No moment people would record and share. The most dramatic thing on the page is the blue row wipe plus the cursor-following preview card, which is the 2018 Codrops hover-reveal pattern.
The intro is a blue curtain with three mono words that wipes away after 0.3s. It is a loader that shows nothing of the system, and then the hero letters simply rise.

The preview card has a soft drop shadow and a velocity tilt: the only soft, skeuomorphic object on an otherwise flat printed page. In the row-hover screenshots the 'VIEW' disc sits on top of the hovered title ('AT_AS FREIGHT').
The manifesto uses an opacity word-fill, the most common scroll-text trick, and doesn't use the variable font at all, even though variable type is the brand.

Services pin: at 1440×900 each panel has roughly 250px of empty ink between the outline numeral and the heading. The numerals are the only motion, and the long pinned scroll carries about 6 lines of content per panel.
The footer punchline 'LET'S MAKE SOMETHING LOUD' just repeats the hero effect at a bigger size. Nothing loud actually happens.
The cursor is the default creative-portfolio white difference disc with a 'VIEW' label, and it switches to a paper disc over blue, so there are two cursor styles.
On phones the page is a static long scroll apart from the tapes, the inline art and touch-morphing in the hero. Taps and swipes have no payoff.
The case sheet has no continuity: the sheet grows from the row band, but a different title fades in. The 62% multiply art behind it turns the IKB into muddy navy rings.
The count-up stats are generic portfolio filler.
hero: COMPOSITION (1440×900): keep the v1 layout: '+' registration marks, the mono spec row (Name / Discipline / Based / Local time), the full-width fitted 4BOOSER line, and the tagline row ('I build interfaces that move.' / availability / scroll cue). Add a specimen ruler directly under the name. It is a 1px baseline with a tick at every letter boundary, and the ticks move with the letters. Under each letter sits a 10.5px mono readout, 'WD 132 / WT 812', with two micro-bars (wdth and wght as 1px bars, 0–48px). At the ruler's left end: '(FIG.1) STRING — 7 NODES · K 220 · ζ .12'. At its right end: 'PLUCK ⟷'. INTERACTION: the name is a damped wave chain whose displacement has zero mean, so the line width is conserved: when one letter swells the others condense, like an accordion, and the line always fills the measure. The cursor's horizontal velocity plucks the letters under it: rightward strokes swell them, leftward strokes condense them. The wave travels, bounces off both ends of the word and dies out in about 1.5s. Letters lean (skewX ±12°) in proportion to wave velocity, so the crest visibly travels. v1's proximity bulge stays on top. Scroll velocity plucks the first letter, so scrolling makes the name ripple. The optional sound toggle makes each letter a Karplus–Strong string tuned to a pentatonic note. The cursor becomes a registration crosshair with a mono label 'PLUCK · X 0812 Y 0344'. INTRO (no curtain): at t=0 the content is fully readable, with letters at hairline wdth 50 / wght 100. At t=150ms an impulse plucks '4'; the crest runs through B-O-O-S-E-R, bounces back once and settles to rest by about 1.6s while the readouts count up from 000. At t=900ms the first Klein drop lands right of centre, over 'SER' and the tagline. It blooms IKB, the letters under it print gold, it dries into halftone by about 2s and is gone by about 5s. That teaches FIG.2 without a word. PHONE (390×844): two fitted lines '4BOO / SER' form one chain that wraps across the line break, with zero mean per line. With touch-action pan-y, a horizontal swipe over the name plucks it while vertical scroll stays native. A tap plucks the tapped letter and drops pigment there. Scroll velocity plucks the first letter. A slow idle drive keeps a gentle ripple. Readouts are 9.5px mono under each line (4 + 3). The intro is the same pluck plus a drop near the tagline. REDUCED MOTION: rest state, no intro, no pigment, static readouts, plain h1 text kept for accessibility.

moves.name: FIG.1 — Plucked String (live type specimen hero)
moves.section: Hero (the same chain engine is reused for the email on copy and for the Kinetik playground)
moves.experience: The name behaves like a physical string. Flick across it and a crest of extra width and weight runs through 4BOOSER, bounces off the ends and dies out, with letters leaning into the motion. Moving slowly gives v1's proximity bulge. Scrolling ripples it. Mono readouts under every letter show live wdth/wght and micro-bars, so the hero reads as a live type-specimen sheet. With sound on, each letter plucks a tuned note. Copying the email plucks the email the same way.
moves.implementation: Float32Arrays u, v, f with N=7. Semi-implicit Euler substeps at h=1/240: a_i = K(u_{i-1} − 2u_i + u_{i+1}) − K0·u_i − C·v_i + f_i, free ends (u_{-1}=u_0, u_N=u_{N-1}), K=220, K0=38, C=7. After each step subtract the per-line mean of u so the measure is conserved; v1's scaleX fit only corrects the leftover non-linearity. Forcing per pointermove: vx = smoothed Δx/Δt in px/ms; f_i += exp(−((xc_i − px)/(0.9·fs))²)·vx·60, gated by |py − lineCentre| < 0.8·lineH. Scroll: f_0 += vel·0.4. Tap: v_i += 6. Mapping: t_i = clamp(M + 0.5·u_i + prox_i, 0, 1), then wdth 50+100t and wght 100+800t (v1's vs()); skewX_i = clamp(v_i·5, −12, 12)deg on each .k span. Readouts: 7 absolutely positioned mono spans, moved each frame with translateX to the letter centres (from the rects v1 already reads in its read phase, writes after). Update their text every 3rd frame; micro-bars use scaleX. Intro: v_0 = +9 at t=150ms. Sound (nav toggle '(Sound ○)', created on that click): precompute 7 Karplus–Strong AudioBuffers (noise burst seed, y[n] = 0.996·0.5·(y[n−P] + y[n−P−1]), P = sr/f, 1.2s, pitches A2 C3 D3 E3 G3 A3 C4). Play one when the impulse on letter i is above 2, with gain ∝ impulse and at most one per letter every 90ms. Sleep when Σ(u² + v²) < 1e−4 and there is no input.
moves.phone: The chain spans both fitted lines (4BOO / SER), coupled across the break, with zero mean per line. With pan-y on the hero, horizontal swipes pluck, taps pluck the tapped letter (and drop pigment there), and vertical scroll stays native and still plucks through scroll velocity. Readouts are 9.5px. The idle auto-drive (v1 'auto' mode) feeds the chain at low amplitude.
moves.perf_and_fallback: 7 nodes cost almost nothing. The real cost is re-shaping 7 glyphs plus one forced layout read per frame, which v1 already pays. The loop sleeps when the chain is at rest. Reduced motion: rest axes, no intro, static readouts. No JS: plain h1. AudioContext only exists after the toggle click, so there are no autoplay issues.

moves.name: Riso Plates — misregistered slit-scan preview card + plate slip on display type
moves.section: Selected Work (card), section titles, skill tapes, footer lines (plate slip)
moves.experience: Hovering a row brings up a flat card: no shadow, no tilt, '+' crop marks at the corners and a mono caption '03 — Atlas Freight · 2 plates'. The art is printed as two riso plates, ink and IKB, which overprint to navy where they overlap. The blue plate is always about 1px out of register and slips further with cursor speed. A fast flick across the rows tears the card in time: its lower rows trail behind the top, like a sheet dragged across a scanner glass, then snap back into register when you stop. Fast page scrolls make big display type do the same: a blue plate peeks out under the ink letters by up to 8px and re-registers as scrolling slows. This replaces the generic RGB-split with the print equivalent in the brand's own two colours.
moves.implementation: Refactor ART[i](c, w, h, t, plate) to draw one plate on transparent. Plate 'k' draws the ink shapes in #0E0E10. Plate 'b' draws the IKB shapes in #1D2CF3, with paper-coloured elements cut out using globalCompositeOperation 'destination-out'. Use two offscreen canvases for the active project at card size. The visible card canvas is the card plus 120px padding left and right. Per frame: fill paper; set gco = 'multiply'; for j in 0..39 strips (sh = h/40), lagX = hist[(head − round(j·0.35)) & 63] − cardX, then drawImage(plateB, 0, j·sh, w, sh, PAD + lagX + misX, j·sh + misY, w, sh) and drawImage(plateK, …, PAD + lagX, j·sh). hist is a 64-entry ring buffer of the card's x position, one entry per frame. mis = (1, 0.5)px base plus clamp(cursorVel·0.12, ±14px). Card position follows v1 (parked beside the title, never on it). Display slip: set one root CSS var --mis = clamp(scrollVel·0.35, −8, 8) per frame. .sec-title, .mq-unit, .foot-lines use text-shadow: 0 calc(var(--mis)·1px) 0 var(--blue); on blue zones the shadow uses the ink colour. Write it only when |vel| > 1.5, otherwise set 'none'.
moves.phone: There is no hover card. The inline .r-media canvases use the same plates, and the blue plate slips vertically with scroll velocity, so riso misregistration happens as you scroll. No slit-scan on phones. Tapping a row triggers the title lift.
moves.perf_and_fallback: Two plate draws plus 80 strip drawImage calls take well under 1ms, and the canvas only redraws while the card is visible. The text-shadow repaint happens only during fast scrolls; turn it off on phones if the frame-time governor reports more than 20ms. Reduced motion: plates in register, static frame, no slip. If canvas is unavailable, the row wipe still works.

moves.name: Title Lift + Kinetik case is the product
moves.section: Work rows → case sheet; Case 05 'Kinetik'
moves.experience: Clicking a row grows the blue sheet out of the row band, as in v1. At the same time the title words themselves lift out of the row and fly and scale into the full-screen case title, widening from wdth 112 to 150 during the flight. It is one continuous object with no cross-fade. Closing reverses the flight back into the row. Case 05 (Kinetik, 'variable font playground') is not a write-up but the product itself. It has an editable fitted line ('TYPE ANYTHING') running the FIG.1 string engine, two hairline faders for rest wdth and wght, '● REC 3s', and 'COPY CSS', which exports the recorded motion as per-letter @keyframes to the clipboard. The case study demonstrates the project live.
moves.implementation: Lay out the case first (hidden attribute off, visibility hidden, starting clip band) and run fitCaseTitle. Measure the per-word rects of the row title and the case title (both split into word spans). Create fixed clones in the same font at z 105. For 760ms with ease cubic-bezier(.76,0,.24,1) and a 60ms stagger per word, each frame sets fontSize = lerp(fsRow, fsCase, e), font-variation-settings 'wdth' lerp(112,150,e), 'wght' 900, and transform translate(lerp(x0,x1,e), lerp(capTop0,capTop1,e)), aligning on cap tops (top + 0.08·fs). At the end, show the real title and remove the clones. The sheet's clip-path transition uses the same duration and ease. Do not use View Transitions: they cross-fade bitmaps and can't interpolate axes. Kinetik: a contenteditable='plaintext-only' line, max 16 characters, uppercase via CSS; rebuild the Chain on input. REC samples (wdth, wght) per letter at 30fps for 90 frames. Export with `@keyframes kinetik-${i}{${frames.map((f,k)=>`${(k/89*100).toFixed(1)}%{font-variation-settings:'wdth' ${f.w},'wght' ${f.g}}`).join('')}}`, then copy with v1's clipboard, toast and fallback.
moves.phone: A tap triggers the same lift. Case titles wrap to 2–3 lines and per-word FLIP handles that. Kinetik uses the on-screen keyboard; a swipe on the line plucks it; REC and COPY are full-width mono buttons; the faders are native range inputs styled as hairlines.
moves.perf_and_fallback: 1–3 clones with a per-frame font-size change cost one small relayout per frame for 760ms. Reduced motion: instant sheet with no flight (v1 behaviour), and the Kinetik faders still work with no auto motion. Focus management, Esc and inert stay as in v1.

moves.name: FIG.3 — Re-set Type (spring-held rigid-body footer)
moves.section: Blue footer band 'LET'S MAKE / SOMETHING / LOUD.'
moves.experience: The three fitted lines sit typeset and readable. On first view the full stop drops off the end of 'LOUD.', bounces twice and rolls left: that is the invitation. Every glyph is a rigid body held to its typeset position by a spring. Brushing past makes letters wobble. Hitting them fast, or dragging one and flinging it, snaps it off the line: it tumbles, lands on the lines below (which sag on their springs like a shelf) and piles on the floor. Every impact makes the hit letter bolder: it swells to wght 900 / wdth 150, squashes, then relaxes. With sound on, impacts make letterpress thuds. A mono '(Re-set type)' button springs every letter home in a staggered flight and locks the line again. '(Drop type)' releases them all, which is also the keyboard path. Caption: '(FIG.3) 22 RIGID BODIES — HIT THEM.' The foot bar shows a live lab readout: '60 FPS · STRING 7N · FLUID 128×72 · BODIES 22'.
moves.implementation: Lazy-load https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/matter-js@0.19.0/build/matter.min.js when the band is within 1.5 viewports. Use band-local coordinates. For each glyph span: w = width·0.94, h = 0.70·fs (cap box), centre at the cap middle; Bodies.rectangle with chamfer 3, friction .5, restitution .18, density .0016. Constraint {pointA: home, bodyB, length 0, stiffness .07, damping .12}. While held, add an angular spring: setAngularVelocity(b, ω·.9 − angle·.08). Add static floor, walls and a ceiling at the band edges; the floor is the bottom of the headline block, above the contact grid. DOM: transform translate(x−hx, y−hy) rotate(a), with transform-origin at the body centre. Do not use Matter.MouseConstraint: in 0.19 its Mouse calls preventDefault on wheel and touch, which kills page scroll. Write your own drag instead: pointerdown on a glyph creates a Constraint {pointA: pointer, bodyB, stiffness .25}; release passes on the pointer velocity. Knock: if pointer speed > 1.6px/ms, Query.ray(heldBodies, p0, p1, 10), then remove the spring and setVelocity(pointer v·14 with a small upward kick) plus random spin. Loudness: on collisionStart, relSpeed gives L = max(L, v/14), decaying 2.5/s; wght = 500+400L, wdth = 100+50L, scaleY(1 − .18L) for 120ms. Thud: noise → bandpass(140 + 260·(1−L)) → 60ms envelope. Re-set: set collisionFilter.group = −1, ramp new springs' stiffness from .004 to .07 over 700ms with a 28ms stagger, then restore collisions. When every body is within 0.5px and 0.01rad of home, clear transforms and stop. Fixed step of 1000/60 with an accumulator (max 3 steps), enableSleeping, and run only while the band intersects the viewport.
moves.phone: The lines are fitted at about 60px. Glyphs get touch-action:none and the rest of the band stays pan-y, so swiping between letters scrolls and touching a letter grabs it. A tap knocks a letter off (upward impulse plus spin); a drag throws it. Buttons are full-width mono. No device tilt: the iOS permission prompt isn't worth it.
moves.perf_and_fallback: 22 bodies take about 0.2ms per step plus 22 transform writes; the engine sleeps when everything rests. If the script fails or the page is offline, fall back to v1's static kinetic lines. Reduced motion: no physics, no falling full stop, buttons hidden. Accessibility: the h2 aria-label stays, glyphs are aria-hidden, the buttons are real <button>s. On resize, re-set first, then rebuild home positions. The band uses overflow: clip, so there is no horizontal scroll.

moves.name: FIG.2 — Klein Pigment (IKB / Monogold screen-print fluid) — signature move
moves.section: Global layer over the whole page; it reads best on the manifesto paper field, gold on the ink services section, navy and gold on blue areas
moves.experience: Anywhere on the page, a fast flick of the cursor lays down a stroke of Klein pigment. Press-and-drag pours; a click drops a blot that blooms into curling tendrils. Under the pigment the page prints in negative. On paper, the paper turns IKB #002FA7 and every ink letter under it turns gold #D8AA2C: Klein's IKB and Monogold. On the ink services section it becomes a gold field with IKB type. On the blue band, the blue row wipes and the case sheet it becomes deep navy #0F113C with gold type. The pigment is wet for about 1s (solid, crisp screen-print edge), then dries into a 45° halftone fixed to the page whose dots shrink to nothing over about 4s. It is stuck to the paper: scroll and the stain moves with the content, and in the pinned services section it moves sideways with the track. Slow reading movements deposit nothing, so text is never covered at rest. The cursor is a registration crosshair labelled with the current action (PAINT / PLUCK / OPEN / THROW) and page coordinates. Caption next to the manifesto: '(FIG.2) KLEIN PIGMENT — FLICK TO PAINT · 128×72 GRID'.
moves.implementation: Fixed <canvas> inset 0, z-index 101 (above the case sheet and the grain, below the cursor and toast), pointer-events none, WebGL2 context with alpha:false (black is a no-op under difference), mix-blend-mode: difference. Stable fluids (Stam '99, Dobryakov pipeline): velocity RG16F at sim resolution 128 (short side), dye R16F at 512, plus curl, divergence and pressure (Jacobi). Fall back across R16F → RG16F → RGBA16F render formats. Per frame: splats → curl → vorticity confinement (ε 26: f = normalize(0.5·(|ω_T|−|ω_B|, |ω_R|−|ω_L|))·ε·ω, y flipped) → divergence → pressure ×0.8 then 20 Jacobi passes, p = (L+R+B+T − div)/4 → subtract gradient → advect velocity (dissipation .25) → advect dye (dissipation .6/s) → display. Keeping it fixed to the page: every advect samples c = vUv − dt·vel·texel − uShift, where uShift is (Δtrack_x/W, Δscroll_y/H) in GL y-up coordinates (vertical scroll normally, ΔhsX while the services pin is active, the case-scroll delta when the case is open). Return 0 when c is outside [0,1] so edges don't smear. Splat: o = src + exp(−dot(p,p)/r)·col, with p.x scaled by aspect. Emission: dye = min(.9, max(0, speed − 0.6px/ms)·0.35) at r = .0018·(1 + speed·.5); press-drag deposits 1.0; a click is a drop: dye 1.4 at r .005 plus 10 radial velocity splats at radius .02 with |v| 900 and jitter. Emission gain is .35 over work rows and 1 elsewhere. Display shader: solid = smoothstep(.5−fw, .5+fw, d) with fw = fwidth(d)·.75. Dot radius r = .5·sqrt(clamp((d−.06)/.44, 0, 1)) on a 7-CSS-px grid rotated 45°, with grid coordinates offset by the accumulated uShift so the dots stay fixed to the page. a = max(solid, dot). Output vec4(D·a, 1). D is chosen per region: D_paper = (230,184,60)/255 gives |paper−D| = #002FA7 and |ink−D| = #D8AA2C. Inside blue rectangles (uniform vec4[6]: footer band, blue Motion panel, hovered row, case sheet; read each frame from cached elements) D_blue = (14,61,183)/255 gives blue → #0F113C and paper → #D8AA2C. Verified contrast: IKB/gold 4.9:1, navy/gold 8.3:1. Idle: 6s after the last splat, stop the simulation, clear, and set the canvas to visibility:hidden so the compositor drops the full-screen blend.
moves.phone: Pointer events stop once the browser takes over the pan (pointercancel), so phones don't paint while scrolling. A tap (pointerup without pointercancel, not on a/button/[data-noink]) drops a blot. Horizontal swipes inside the hero and footer (pan-y) paint. The intro's automatic drop teaches the gesture. Sim resolution 64, dye 256, 10 Jacobi passes, DPR 1, halftone cell 5px.
moves.perf_and_fallback: On desktop, about 1–1.5ms GPU at 128/512 plus one full-screen display pass at DPR ≤ 1.5, and the blend layer exists only while pigment exists. Frame-time governor: if the 60-frame average exceeds 20ms, halve the dye resolution and drop the halftone; if it is still slow, turn the feature off. No WebGL2 or no renderable half-float format: feature off (the crosshair cursor stays). prefers-reduced-motion: off. Known issue: small accent-blue italic words on paper print mauve #C98CB7 under pigment. That is transient and acceptable, or add their rects to the blue-rect uniform. Everything decays back to the untouched page in 5s or less.

page_sequence: Nav: mono, difference blend; logo, Work / Services / Contact, a '(Sound ○)' toggle and the 000% progress readout.

Hero = FIG.1 plucked string: spec row, fitted 4BOOSER with the live axis ruler and readouts, tagline row. The intro is the pluck at 150ms plus the first Klein drop at 900ms (FIG.2 teaser). Content is readable from t=0.
Skill tapes: v1's rigid crossing tapes kept, with riso plate slip on scroll velocity replacing skewX.

About: manifesto set from keyline to ink by scroll (replacing opacity), with the '(FIG.2) Klein pigment — flick to paint' caption. This large paper field is where the pigment reads best. Stats are static, no count-up.

Selected Work: index rows with the blue wipe. Desktop gets the misregistered slit-scan riso card on hover; phones get inline plate art that slips while scrolling. Click or tap lifts the title into the case sheet. Case 05 Kinetik is the live playground with REC and COPY CSS.
Services: the horizontal pin on ink with the dead space tightened. Pigment prints Monogold here (gold field, IKB type) and moves sideways with the track.
Footer band = FIG.3 Re-set type: the full stop falls on entry, letters can be hit and thrown, '(Re-set type)' and '(Drop type)' buttons, contact grid below. Pigment prints navy and gold here.
Foot bar: © 2026, demo-content note, a live lab readout (fps · active simulations), back to top.
cut_or_change: CUT the blue curtain intro. The intro becomes the FIG.1 pluck plus the first Klein drop on live, readable content.

CUT the white difference disc cursor with the 'VIEW' label (and its separate paper-disc style on blue). Replace it with one registration crosshair (difference, hairline) plus a mono label showing the current action (PAINT / PLUCK / OPEN ↗ / THROW) and page coordinates, offset so it never covers the hovered title.
CUT the preview card's drop shadow and velocity tilt. It becomes a flat riso plate card with crop marks.

SEED: the fluid simulation is accepted but changed. A soft, dye-coloured fluid is the most-copied WebGL effect around (and close to variant A's nebula). The brand-safe version is a hard-threshold screen-print edge plus halftone that stays fixed to the page, with exact IKB/gold colours through the solved difference colour, stuck to the paper and decaying in about 5s. A plain difference layer cannot turn paper blue and ink gold at the same time; solving D per region can, and the maths is verified above.
SEED: 'slot-machine width reel' intro is replaced. The pluck intro demonstrates the actual hero physics instead of a scramble effect.
SEED: 'type your name' playground is moved into Case 05 Kinetik, where it is the project itself. This keeps the hero's brand name intact.

SEED: physics footer is reframed. Letters stay typeset and readable on springs and only break loose when hit; impacts make them bolder; '(Re-set type)' is a typesetting pun and the restore path. Use a custom pointer drag, not Matter.MouseConstraint, because in 0.19 it calls preventDefault on wheel and touch.

SEED: SVG textPath wavy tapes are rejected. Wavy ribbons are soft candy against rigid brutalist tape, and per-frame textPath re-layout with variable axes is a risk on Safari. Keep v1's rigid crossing tapes and add plate slip.
SEED: WebGL liquid / RGB-split work previews are rejected. It is the 2018 Codrops cliché, and RGB is not this palette. Replace with two-plate riso misregistration plus slit-scan in plain 2D canvas.
SEED: z-space type tunnel is rejected. A 3D camera fly-through breaks the flat printed-sheet idea, adds a second pinned section and more scroll length, and is weak on phones.

SEED: GSAP is dropped. A single rAF loop is already the architecture. Lenis 1.1.13 is used on desktop only: driven from the main loop with lenis.raf(t), remove html{scroll-behavior:smooth}, add data-lenis-prevent on .case-scroll, call lenis.stop() while the case is open, route anchor links through lenis.scrollTo, and skip it entirely under reduced motion or touch.
SEED: WebAudio is accepted behind a nav toggle: Karplus–Strong strings tuned per hero letter, and letterpress thuds on footer impacts.

CHANGE manifesto: replace the opacity word-fill with a keyline→ink fill (color transparent plus a 1px text-stroke, filling to solid by scroll). It causes no reflow and puts the variable/print idea back.

CHANGE services: remove the roughly 250px empty band in each pinned panel (heading tucked under the numeral, description anchored to it) and shorten the pinned scroll distance. It becomes the Monogold zone for the pigment.
CHANGE case sheet: remove the 62% multiply art behind the title so the IKB stays pure, and move the art into a framed plate block within the case grid.
CUT the stat count-up. Set the numerals statically at wdth 150 / wght 900, or pluck them once on entry using the same chain engine.
KEEP: palette, fonts, spec rows, fitted lines, the row blue wipe, the case sheet clipped from the row, the pinned services, the live clock, 'Copy email', and grain (lower to .10 opacity).

thesis: v1 uses a variable font. v2 should be one. The page becomes "Specimen No. 02, 4BOOSER Variable": the developer is presented as a type family, and its two axes (wdth 50–150, wght 100–900) stand for his range. Each section borrows a real specimen-book convention that also works as portfolio content: Title page (hero, with full metric apparatus and live axis readouts), Waterfall (skills), Text setting (about), In Use (work: one family, five client voices), Instances (the process as a journey through the designspace) and Colophon (contact). The axes stop being a hover trick and become information a visitor can read. Yves Klein comes in as material, not decoration. The cursor is his "living brush" from the Anthropometries: a fluid IKB pigment that turns paper into IKB and ink into Monogold through one difference-blend layer. At the end of the visit, the visitor's own painting is printed as a numbered plate (ANT 4B-xxxx) that they sign. The composition follows a volume score: three fortissimo moments (Title page, Instances, Colophon) with quiet, tightly set passages between them. Each section gets exactly one kinetic verb (lean, whip, ink-up, voice, travel, fall), so no effect is reused and no effect is noise. The headline moves are the Title page and the Anthropometry pigment. The moves below are ranked strictly by wow-per-risk.
v1_weaknesses: The hero follows the 2022–24 Awwwards-folio template: a 4-col meta strip, a giant fitted name, a tagline and a 'Scroll' cue line. The variable axes are the whole concept, but they are never shown as information: no metrics, no values, no designspace. A visitor sees 'letters get fat', not 'a variable font being driven'.

Mid-morph states look like rendering errors, not design. In the phone shot the second O is a hairline between two black O's ('4BO0'), and the '4BOO / SER' break splits the handle at a meaningless point.
Parenthetical mono labels ((Name) (Discipline) (About) (Index) (Email) (Elsewhere) (Year) (Role)…) are the most templated move in the genre. Used 15+ times, they become wallpaper.
The crossing caution-tape marquees with outlined (text-stroke) words are a 2020–21 cliché. A tape is also the least informative way to list skills.
The opacity word-fill manifesto and the count-up stat numerals (6+ / 40+ / 12) are stock patterns. The giant stats are filler.
The work index combines a hover list, a cursor-following floating card and a 96px difference 'VIEW' disc, the most copied portfolio trio. At 1024–1280px the card also sits on top of row meta.
The five generative previews share no visual language (op-art waves, rings, warped grid, halftone moon, weight specimen). They read as five screensavers, not one art-directed system.

Services is a pinned horizontal scroll with outline numerals 01–04 and generic copy. Each panel has about 250px of dead space between numeral and title (qa-b-verify-final-desktop-s50), and the exit frame is messy: the CTA box is clipped under the nav (s75).

There is no volume score. The hero name, tapes, WORK, MOVES and LOUD all shout at about 12–19vw, so nothing feels loud. The footer reuses the hero's exact proximity morph, so the finale never escalates.
IKB is used as a flat UI fill (row wipe, panel, band, case sheet): a brand blue, not Klein's pigment. There is no material quality, no gold and no ritual.
The intro is a generic preloader curtain (blue panel plus three mono words) and says nothing about type.
hero:
CONCEPT: the title page of "Specimen No. 02, 4BOOSER Variable". The name is shown the way a font editor shows glyphs: with its metric apparatus and live axis values.

DESKTOP (1440×900; 12 cols, 40px margins, 16px gutters; height 100svh):
• y 0–56, nav: left, a '4B' monogram (wdth 150 wght 900) plus mono 'Specimen No. 02'; centre, Work / Services / Contact; right, the folio 'p. 01/06 Title' and a 'Pigment ●' toggle.
• y 72: one ink hairline. y 82–118: mono 11px header on cols 1/4/7/10, with index numerals instead of parentheses: '01 4BOOSER VARIABLE — Creative Developer' · '02 AXES — wdth 50–150 · wght 100–900' · '03 SET IN — Remote, worldwide' · '04 SET AT — 14:16:01 UTC' (live clock). The registration '+' marks stay at the ends of the rule. A 56px Monogold #D4AF37 'No.02' seal sits rotated −8° at col 12, overlapping the rule.
• y 150–610, glyph stage: 4BOOSER fitted edge to edge (about 1360px). THE REST STATE IS A RAMP, not a uniform instance. Glyph i sits at t=i/6, giving wdth 50+100t and wght 100+800t, so the word reads as an axis diagram: a hairline condensed '4' swelling into a black extended 'R'.
  – Around it, a 1px apparatus: baseline (ink 100%), cap-height line (ink 30%), 2px overshoot bands at cap and baseline (IKB 35%), and 8 vertical advance boundaries (ink 18%) running from cap−28px to baseline+28px.
  – In the right margin, 9px mono labels 'CAP', 'BASE 0' and 'O/S' with values measured from the font. At the top of each boundary, the advance width in font units ('adv 486').
• y 626–672, readout row: one cell per glyph, aligned to its advance box. Three lines of 10px IBM Plex Mono, tabular and zero-padded so the digits never jitter: 'B  U+0042' / 'wdth 083.3' / 'wght 367'. At rest these ticking numbers are the animation.
• y 720–860, bottom band: cols 1–6 hold the tagline 'I build interfaces that move.' (56px, wdth 68 wght 560; 'move.' in IKB italic wdth 150 wght 900). Cols 7–9 hold an IKB dot plus 'Booking Q1 2027'. Cols 10–12 hold a 180×120 'Designspace' plot: hairline square, ticks at 50/100/150 × 100/500/900, 7 dots labelled with their glyph, and an IKB polyline through them. It is the name, plotted live.

INTERACTION:
• Proximity (v1's Gaussian) pulls nearby glyphs toward wide/black.
• Horizontal pointer velocity adds a synthetic slant (skewX ±12°, weighted by proximity) and pushes neighbours apart (translateX up to 0.15em).
• While letters are displaced, tiny IKB tags appear between pairs ('kern +31'). The readout shows 'slnt −8.4*', with the footnote in the colophon: synthetic.
• The pigment brush paints at the same time, so glyphs under pigment turn Monogold on IKB.
• Idle for more than 2.6s: the ramp breathes. Its direction rotates (thin→fat ↔ fat→thin) over about 7s and the readouts tick. Idle for more than 9s: rest.

INTRO (at most 1.6s; any input skips it; none under reduced motion):
• 0–300ms: the baseline and cap lines draw left to right and the guide labels type in.
• 250–1000ms: each advance box opens and its glyph spins through a vertical slot reel of 5 instances (50/100 → 150/900), clipped to the box. It lands on its ramp instance with about 6% overshoot, at a 60ms stagger, while the readouts odometer-count to their values.
• 1000–1400ms: one pigment splat blooms from the '4' and dissipates over about 1.2s, so the page signs itself in IKB and gold. The header types in.
• This replaces v1's blue curtain.

PHONE (390×844):
• Nav 52px. The header becomes 2 mono lines: '4BOOSER VARIABLE — SPECIMEN NO. 02' / 'CREATIVE DEVELOPER · 14:16 UTC'.
• Then 'Fig. 4': the numeral alone at about 300px cap height, wdth 150 wght 900, in its glyph box with metric lines, filling the left 62%. The right 38% column holds its readout (U+0034 / wdth / wght / adv) and a 120×120 designspace plot.
• Below, 'BOOSER' is fitted full width (about 100px) and continues the ramp downward (B 130/800 → R 50/100), with a 2-line 10px readout strip under each glyph.
• Then the tagline (32px) and availability. Everything fits in about 780px.
• Touch: a horizontal drag over the name (touch-action: pan-y) moves the proximity wave. When the name is not being touched, an autopilot wave crosses it every 4s or so, so it stays alive without hover. Scrolling vertically through the hero scrubs the ramp direction. A tap anywhere leaves a pigment blot.
• The '4 | BOOSER' split replaces v1's '4BOO / SER'.

moves.name: Specimen apparatus (running heads, folios, footnotes, grid key)
moves.section: Global: nav plus the head and foot of every section; footnotes in the colophon
moves.experience:
The whole page reads as one printed specimen.
• Each section opens with a mono running head with dot leaders ('4B—02  WATERFALL ………… 10 STYLES') and closes with a folio number at the bottom right.
• The nav's 000% becomes 'p. 02/06 Waterfall'.
• All parenthetical labels become index numerals ('01 Name', '02 Discipline').
• Readouts carry footnote marks that are resolved in the colophon:
  – '* slnt is synthetic. Anybody ships a real italic; we skew because we're impatient.'
  – '† 101 × 801 = 80,901 integer instances. We tried them all.'
  – '‡ No glyphs were harmed. Several were stretched.'
• Pressing G overlays the 12-col grid and the 8px baseline grid with a spec caption ('12 cols · 16 gutter · baseline 8').
• Monogold appears statically in only two places: the 'No.02' edition seal and this caption's swatch.
moves.implementation:
• Sections get data-folio='02' and data-title='Waterfall'. The nav folio is resolved from v1's cached [data-nav] zones (no per-frame layout reads).
• Running head: a flex row whose filler is background: radial-gradient(circle, currentColor 1px, transparent 1.5px) 0 70% / 8px 8px repeat-x.
• Grid overlay: a fixed, aria-hidden div with two repeating-linear-gradients. Columns are computed from the CSS gutter vars; baseline rows are 8px at 6% ink. Toggled on keydown 'g', ignored when focus is in inputs or contenteditable.
• Footnotes: plain markup in the colophon; the marks in readouts are <sup>.
• Seal: a 56px circle in #D4AF37 with mono 'No.02' in ink, rotate(-8deg).
moves.phone:
• Running heads collapse to one line ('4B—02 WATERFALL').
• The nav hides the folio for space; each section still shows its own folio.
• The grid overlay toggles with a 500ms long-press on the nav monogram.
• Footnotes are unchanged.
moves.perf_and_fallback: Effectively zero cost (static markup and CSS). Without JS, everything except the nav folio and the grid key still renders. Unaffected by reduced motion.

moves.name: Title page: live specimen hero
moves.section: Hero, 4B—01 (full composition in the hero field)
moves.experience:
• 4BOOSER is set as a weight/width ramp inside a font-editor apparatus: baseline, cap and overshoot lines, advance boxes, and per-glyph mono readouts (U+, wdth, wght, adv) that tick live.
• A 180×120 designspace plot shows the 7 glyphs as dots.
• The cursor pulls glyphs toward black/extended by proximity. Its horizontal speed shears them (synthetic slant, footnoted) and pushes pairs apart, with 'kern +31' tags.
• While idle, the ramp breathes.
• The intro is a construction sequence (guides draw, slot reels of instances land, one pigment splat signs the page) instead of a curtain.
• On phones the composition is 'Fig. 4' plus 'BOOSER'.
moves.implementation:
Extend v1's Kinetic class (it already reads glyph rects every frame):
(a) The rest target becomes a ramp, t_i = i/(n−1) → (wdth 50+100t, wght 100+800t). Idle 'auto' mode rotates it: t_i' = .5 + (t_i − .5)·cos(now·.0009).
(b) Pointer vx is an EMA over about 80ms. Per letter: skewX = clamp(−vx·.5, −12, 12)·w_i deg; translateX = sign(x_i − px)·w_i·min(|vx|·.6px, .15em). Both go on the .k span as transforms (no reflow). A kern tag shows when |dx| > 4px.
(c) The apparatus is an absolutely positioned layer over the h1: 8 boundary hairlines (translateX), 3 horizontal guides and labels.
  – The baseline comes from a zero-height inline-block probe span in the line.
  – Cap and overshoot ratios come once, after fonts.ready, from canvas measureText('H'/'O').actualBoundingBoxAscent at 1000px.
  – adv = rect.width / fontSize × 1000 / lineScaleX.
  – Readout text nodes are written only when their cached string changes, zero-padded with tabular figures.
(d) The designspace plot is inline SVG (7 circles, 7 texts, 1 polyline), updated only on moving frames.
(e) The intro is a hand-rolled timeline. Each .k temporarily hosts 5 stacked instance spans inside an overflow:clip box, translated in Y with ease-out-back. Then the pigment layer gets one splat at the '4'. pointerdown, keydown or wheel completes the timeline instantly.
moves.phone:
• The '4' becomes a ~300px Fig. 4 in its glyph box (left 62%), with its readout and a 120px plot on the right.
• BOOSER is fitted full width below, ramp 130/800 → 50/100, each glyph with a 2-line readout.
• Touch: horizontal drag over the name (touch-action: pan-y) steers the wave. An autopilot wave runs every 4s when untouched. Vertical scroll scrubs the ramp direction. A tap leaves a pigment blot.
• The intro is shortened to 1.2s.
moves.perf_and_fallback:
• Per frame: 7 rect reads (already in v1), up to 7 font-variation-settings writes, up to 16 transforms, and text writes only when values change. About 0.6ms; nothing runs once v1's 'still' flag settles.
• Reduced motion: the ramp and readouts are static, with no intro and no velocity.
• Without JS: a plain fitted h1 at a uniform instance.

moves.name: Waterfall: width-axis line fitting with a scroll whip
moves.section: Skills, 4B—02 (replaces both marquee tapes)
moves.experience:
• A classic specimen waterfall: ten lines, one skill each, with sizes stepping down a 0.8 geometric scale (TYPESCRIPT at about 13vw down to CREATIVE CODING at about 1.8vw). Weight descends from 900 to 300 down the cascade.
• A mono left gutter gives each line's spec ('144 PT · wdth 061 · wght 900').
• After each skill name, a lowercase sample phrase in wdth 100 wght 300 runs off the right edge, as specimens do ('TypeScript — strict types, loose ideas').
• Every skill name fits the measure exactly because the WIDTH AXIS does the line-fitting, not tracking or font-size: big lines compress themselves and small ones expand.
• Scroll fast and a squeeze wave whips down the cascade, each line lagging the one above. At rest the page is perfectly set.
• Hover a line: it eases to wght 900 at its max-fit width and its spec label turns IKB.
moves.implementation:
• Ten nowrap

lines in an overflow:clip section, each with contain: layout paint. • Layout pass (on fonts.ready and resize): font-size_i = base·0.8^i (base 13vw desktop, 19vw phone). Binary-search wdth_i (7 iterations, offsetWidth of the name span) for the largest value ≤150 that fits the measure minus the label column. Then write the labels. • Motion: a 10-node spring chain. – node0 target = clamp(scrollVelocity/40, −1, 1). – Each node follows the one above: a_i += (a_{i−1} − a_i)·(1 − .82^dt). • Each line writes wdth_i·(1 − .35|a_i|) (squeeze only, so names never overflow), wght + 180|a_i|, and skewX(−7a_i deg). • Only lines with |a_i| > .002 write.
moves.phone:
• Same structure. Base 19vw, so TYPESCRIPT compresses to about wdth 55 to fit 358px.
• The four largest lines get their spec as a 2-line 9px mono stack above-left; the rest keep it inline.
• The whip is driven by touch-scroll velocity.
• Sample phrases are clipped at the gutter, so there is no horizontal page scroll.
moves.perf_and_fallback:
• Up to 10 font-variation-settings writes per frame, only while scrolling: about 0.3ms.
• Reduced motion: a static waterfall at the solved widths.
• Without JS: CSS fallback wdth values per line.
• Readable at rest by construction.

moves.name: Your Anthropometry: the visit printed as a signed plate
moves.section: Colophon, 4B—06 (after contact, inside the IKB band)
moves.experience:
• A paper plate hangs on the IKB band like a print on a gallery wall (3:4): 'ANT 4B–0427 (Untitled Anthropometry), 2026'.
• It shows the visitor's own path through the page. Every cursor stroke and tap from the visit is rendered as IKB pigment and mapped by document position: hero scribbles sit at the top of the plate, footer strokes at the bottom.
• Mono caption: 'Pigment on screen. 3 min 12 s. 18,204 px of stroke. 41 blots. Signed: ________'.
• The signature line is an inline editable field (the 'type your name' seed, relocated), set in Anybody italic wdth 120 wght 700. Its letters morph with the cursor like the hero.
• 'Re-paint' replays the strokes as a 4-second timelapse.
• Klein's Anthropometries used bodies as living brushes; here the visitor is the brush.
moves.implementation:
• Recording: on pointermove, store {x/innerWidth, (scrollY+y)/docHeight, t, tap}, throttled to 30ms with a 6px minimum distance. Cap at 6000 points and decimate ×2 when full.
• Drawing, on colophon enter, into a 2D canvas (DPR ≤2):
  – segments with lineCap round, lineWidth = clamp(18 − speed·.4, 2, 18)·scale, in IKB;
  – taps as jittered 12-gon blots;
  – then a pre-generated 256px noise pattern filled with globalCompositeOperation 'multiply' at 25%, for pigment grain.
• Plate number: hash(visit start) mod 10000.
• Signature: a contenteditable='plaintext-only' span (spellcheck off, 24-char limit enforced in JS), default 'Anonymous visitor'. It is re-split into .k spans on input and fed to the Kinetic engine.
• Replay: segments are drawn progressively with rAF over 4s.
• Nothing is persisted.
moves.phone:
• Records touch drags and taps.
• The plate is full width (358×477) under the contact block.
• Focusing the signature opens the keyboard, and the plate scrolls into view above it.
• With fewer than 20 points, the plate shows the intro splat plus the hint 'Tap anywhere above to paint', so it is never empty.
moves.perf_and_fallback:
• A one-off draw of about 5ms; replay only on demand.
• Reduced motion: drawn statically, replay hidden.
• Independent of WebGL. It still records and prints if the pigment layer is off or unsupported.

moves.name: Instances: the process as a journey through the designspace
moves.section: Services, 4B—05 (replaces the pinned horizontal panels)
moves.experience:
• The four stages are named instances of the family:
  – STRATEGY = Thin Compressed (wdth 50 · wght 100)
  – DESIGN = Regular (75 · 400)
  – DEVELOP = Bold (112.5 · 700)
  – MOTION = Black Extended (150 · 900)
  The project literally gets louder as it moves.
• Pinned stage on ink, left 7 cols: one giant word fitted to the column, its axes interpolating continuously with scroll. At each stage boundary its letters split-flap through random capitals into the next word.
• Right 5 cols: a 420px designspace plot. Hairline square with ticks; the four instances as labelled nodes; an IKB path drawn progressively with scroll; a live dot with crosshairs to both axes and a mono readout 'wdth 112.4 · wght 668'.
• Under the plot, the stage copy and deliverables crossfade.
• At the last node the dot bursts: an IKB circle expands from it and floods the stage, so the page becomes a Klein monochrome and flows straight into the IKB colophon.
moves.implementation:
• Section height 420vh; the .stage is sticky at top 0 with height 100svh.
• Progress p maps to the path parameter with a 15% dwell at each node (smoothstep between), so every stage rests readable.
• Word: one nowrap line. Font-size per word is precomputed at layout so it fills cols 1–7 at its own node's instance. Between nodes, font-size and axes lerp, and v1's scaleX correction absorbs the residual width.
• Split-flap: in a 0.2 band around each boundary, every letter slot swaps through 4 random A–Z glyphs (textContent every 50ms, 30ms stagger left to right) and then lands. Surplus slots collapse to wdth 50 and opacity 0.
• Plot: inline SVG. The path has pathLength=1 and stroke-dashoffset = 1 − p; the dot, two crosshair lines and the readout update per frame.
• Flood: clip-path: circle(r at x y) on an IKB layer, driven by p over the last 8%.
• All four stages exist as a real list in the DOM for screen readers; the visual word is aria-hidden.
moves.phone:
• Also pinned (100svh, 320vh of scroll): the word on top, fitted to 358px; the plot as a centred 220px square; one sentence plus inline deliverables below.
• If innerHeight < 620 or reduced motion: an un-pinned stack, each stage word set statically in its instance with a 120px static plot marking its node.
moves.perf_and_fallback:
• One font-variation-settings write plus about 6 SVG attribute writes per frame: under 0.3ms. Runs only while the section intersects the viewport.
• Optional lenis@1.1.13 on desktop only (smoothWheel, no syncTouch) makes the axis travel buttery; native sticky is unaffected.
• Fallback: the static stack.

moves.name: Re-set type: the spring-homed physics headline and the Hellbox
moves.section: Colophon headline, 4B—06 (IKB band)
moves.experience:
• The headline is a typographic crescendo: LET'S MAKE (wdth 50 · wght 300) / SOMETHING (100 · 600) / LOUD. (150 · 900).
• When the band enters, the letters drop from above and are caught by springs in their typeset positions. LOUD. lands last and heaviest, with a bigger bounce.
• Every letter hangs on an invisible spring to its home:
  – sweep the cursor through and the letters scatter and swing back like jelly type;
  – grab one and throw it, and it stretches wider along its speed and flashes to wght 900 on impact.
• The mono button 'Drop the type' cuts the springs. Everything crashes to the floor of the band and piles up, captioned 'Hellbox: 23 sorts' (the letterpress box for spent type).
• The button becomes 'Re-set type ↺' and the letters fly home.
• At rest the headline always reads perfectly.
moves.implementation:
• matter-js@0.19.0 (cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/matter-js@0.19.0/build/matter.min.js), loaded lazily when the band is within one viewport.
• Letters stay DOM spans (crisp; the h2 keeps its aria-label).
• At layout, measure each span rect → Bodies.rectangle(advance × cap-height, chamfer 4, density ∝ wght) + a Constraint to a static home point (stiffness .02, damping .1, length 0).
• Entry: bodies start 100vh above home with gravity on; spring stiffness ramps 0→.02 over 500ms.
• Pointer: a kinematic circle body (r 56) moved with Body.setPosition/setVelocity each frame. MouseConstraint handles grab and throw on fine pointers.
• Walls and floor: static bodies on the band bounds.
• Render: span.style.transform = translate(x−homeX, y−homeY) rotate(a), plus wdth = base + min(speed·6, 50).
• Stepping: fixed-step Engine.update(1000/60) with an accumulator. Sleeping is enabled; the loop stops when every body sleeps or the band leaves view.
• Drop / Re-set: Composite.remove/add of the constraints. The sort count is computed.
moves.phone:
• No drag, so vertical scrolling is never captured. Tapping a letter flicks it (applyForce upward plus random torque); it tumbles and springs home.
• Drop and Re-set work the same.
• Letters are ≥48px tall, easy targets. touch-action stays pan-y everywhere.
moves.perf_and_fallback:
• 23 bodies: under 0.5ms per step, and nothing while asleep or off-screen.
• If the script fails to load: a static headline with v1's proximity morph.
• Reduced motion: a static typeset headline; the buttons are hidden.

moves.name: Anthropometry: fluid IKB pigment with paper→IKB and ink→Monogold
moves.section: Global layer over the whole page (also over the case sheet)
moves.implementation:
• One fixed full-viewport <canvas>: z 105 (above content and the case sheet, below cursor and intro), pointer-events none, mix-blend-mode: difference.
• Simulation: vanilla WebGL2 stable fluids (Stam semi-Lagrangian, structured like Dobryakov's WebGL-Fluid-Simulation).
  – Velocity grid 128px on the short side; dye 512.
  – Curl/vorticity 10; 16 Jacobi pressure iterations; dye dissipation ≈ .955 per frame.
  – Splats from pointer deltas, at most 3 per frame.
• Scroll compensation: each frame, offset the advection UVs by the scroll delta, so the pigment sticks to the content it painted.
• Display pass: m = smoothstep(.18, .24, dye + (hash(gl_FragCoord.xy) − .5)·.06); out = X(zone)·m.
• X is chosen per pixel from a uniform array of up to 8 viewport-space bands, built each frame from v1's cached [data-nav] zones plus scrollY:
  – paper/ink zones: X = #E2BD00 (paper→#042AE3, ink→#D4AF10);
  – blue zones (colophon, case, Motion flood): X = #F1DBBC (IKB→#D4AF37, paper→#0B0C27).
  Black (no pigment) is the identity under difference.
• Energy tracker: e += splat strength, e *= .955 per frame. When e < .01 for 20 frames, stop the loop and set the canvas to visibility: hidden, so there is no blend cost while reading. The first splat restarts it.
moves.phone:
• Scrolling never paints.
• A tap anywhere drops a blot (radius ×3, no velocity, a little curl).
• Touch drags paint only inside the hero and the colophon. Both use pan-y, so vertical scroll still works.
• Simulation 96 / dye 320, DPR 1.
moves.perf_and_fallback:
• About 1.5–2.5ms of GPU time on an Iris Xe class laptop while active; zero when idle.
• Needs half-float render targets (EXT_color_buffer_half_float / OES_texture_half_float).
  – Fallback A: an RGBA8 diffusion-only version (advect by curl noise plus blur, no pressure solve).
  – Fallback B, no WebGL: three lagging 140px divs with radial-gradient(#E2BD00, transparent 70%) under the same difference blend.
• Reduced motion: off.
• A nav toggle, 'Pigment ●/○', turns it off for anyone.

moves.name: Five voices: instance-set index plus iso-type art in the row band
moves.section: Work, 4B—04 'In Use', plus the case sheet restyled as a 'Plate'
moves.experience:
• The index stays a Swiss table of contents: No. / title / dot leaders / description / year / 'Plate 02 →'.
• Each title is permanently set in its client's own instance, so the list shows typographic range at rest, with no hover needed:
  – AURORA BANK, Light Extended (wdth 150 · wght 250): calm;
  – PULSE RECORDS, Black Compressed (50 · 900): loud;
  – ATLAS FREIGHT, Medium tracked +4% (112.5 · 520): data;
  – Nocturne, thin italic (75 · 160): a whisper;
  – KINETIK, which animates through the whole ramp because it is the font playground.
• A mono line under each title names the instance.
• Hover: no floating card. The row band itself becomes the preview: a full-bleed strip of the project's art wipes in from the entry edge, and the title pushes further along its own direction.
• All five arts are one system, 'iso-type': each is a shader over the signed distance field of the project's name set in its instance.
  – Aurora: drifting iso-line curtains.
  – Pulse: rings radiating from the letter outlines on a 128 bpm envelope.
  – Atlas: a grid displaced by the field, with a dashed route along the outline.
  – Nocturne: halftone dots sized by the field under a slow moon gradient.
  – Kinetik: the field morphing between thin and black instances.
• Click: v1's row-to-sheet clip wipe opens 'Plate 02/05': art full-bleed, the title in its instance, and a specimen table (Instance / Year / Role / Stack / Next plate →).
moves.implementation:
• SDFs, generated in idle time after fonts.ready:
  – Render each name into a 1024×192 canvas using ctx.font weight plus a stretch keyword. The instances sit exactly on keyword stretches (50 / 75 / 112.5 / 150%), so canvas and DOM match; fallback is ctx.scale.
  – Compute a signed squared EDT (Felzenszwalb 1D row and column passes, about 10ms each) and upload it as an R8 texture.
• Rendering: one shared WebGL context and one fragment program with a mode uniform.
  – The canvas is re-parented into the hovered row (the row already has isolation; the canvas at z −1 replaces the blue ::before) and revealed with a clip-path inset from the entry edge.
  – For the Plate, the canvas moves into the sheet at half resolution.
• Palettes are limited to ink/IKB/paper, with low luminance behind the title so paper text holds at least 4.5:1.
moves.phone:
• Rows stack: number + year, the title in its instance, the instance line, the description, then an inline 16:9 art strip.
• The shared context renders each visible strip and drawImage copies it into that row's 2D canvas (at most 2 visible, 30fps, only while at least 50% in view).
• Tap opens the Plate.
moves.perf_and_fallback:
• The shader is about 1 texture fetch plus ~20 ALU ops over roughly 1440×130px: negligible. That makes two WebGL contexts in total, which is fine.
• Without WebGL: v1's 2D canvas arts.
• Reduced motion: one static frame per art, and the hover wipe without animation.

page_sequence: Intro (at most 1.6s, overlaps the Title page): a construction sequence. Guides draw, glyph slot reels spin and land, and one pigment splat signs the page. Skippable on any input; absent under reduced motion.
4B—01 TITLE PAGE (hero, 100svh), fortissimo: 4BOOSER as a live specimen with metric apparatus, axis readouts and a designspace plot; the pigment brush is live.
