thesis: v1 is a deck of good tricks, all played at the same volume. v2 should be one performance with an arc. The whole page becomes a crescendo of one variable font, from a hairline whisper (wght 100) to LOUD (wght 900). The name itself rests on that ramp, so a static screenshot already states the idea, and the footer line 'LET'S MAKE SOMETHING LOUD' pays it off. Every section change is an event made of type instead of a background edge. The hero builds itself in place out of the font-loading state, with no curtain. The first thing your hand touches is Klein pigment that turns paper IKB and ink monogold. The O of MOVES swallows you into the black. A split-flap board clatters through the process stages, with the weight rising at each stage, and then flips the whole screen to International Klein Blue. The finale hands the type to the visitor: they drop their own word into 'LET'S MAKE ___ LOUD', throw the letters around, watch the page put itself back into Swiss order, and rewind the whole film to the start. Rules: scroll-scrubbed transitions can be reversed, triggered events are short and mechanical, nothing important waits on a timer, and everything reads at rest. Phones get their own gestures instead of 'desktop minus hover': multi-touch painting, tape scrubbing, a jog-wheel index, swipe-to-dismiss cases, flinging letters and optional tilt. Sound and haptics are an opt-in, synthesized 'instrument mode' whose filter opens as you scroll down, so the page literally gets louder.
v1_weaknesses: No arc. v1 is a set of strong tricks at equal volume. Nothing builds, and the ending reuses the opening trick (the same Gaussian proximity morph on the footer lines) instead of paying it off.
The intro is a ~1 s blue curtain wiping up over three mono labels and has no link to the hero. The hero then uses the most common reveal there is: letters rising out of a mask.
Colour changes are hard background edges (paper -> ink -> blue). The colour story is never staged as an event.
The manifesto word-opacity fill (words at .28 opacity are also low-contrast) and the stat count-up are the two most worn scroll tropes.

Pinned horizontal services is a generic pattern. Each panel has a ~250px dead void between the numeral and the title (desktop s50 shot), and on phones it collapses into a plain stacked list with no moment at all.

On phones it is 'desktop minus hover': five inline canvases in the index, stacked services, a footer that morphs only in auto mode. No gesture exists only for touch, and the hero reacts only inside its own box.
The cursor is a ~15px difference dot most of the time. The VIEW bubble plus a floating image card is the default 'hover reveal' trope.
The row title and the case title are disconnected. The clip-path grows from the row, but nothing travels, so the best transition loses its continuity.
The two tapes overlap so much that the lower one is half hidden (WEBGL clipped in the shots). Skew is driven by raw scrollY deltas and looks steppy with wheel notches (no smooth scroll).
The ending is passive: a contact grid and a plain 'Back to top' link. There is nothing to do, nothing to remember and no loop.
No sound, no haptics, and no idle storytelling beyond the hero's auto lens.
hero: COMPOSITION (1440x900): fixed difference-blend nav (4BOOSER©26 on the left; WORK / SERVICES / CONTACT in the centre; on the right a 10-bar VU meter 'VOL 000' plus a 'SOUND ○ OFF' toggle). At y≈78, the 1px spec rule with four mono cells: NAME / DISCIPLINE / BASED / LOCAL TIME (the seconds are a small split-flap). Then 4BOOSER, full-bleed and width-fitted with the v1 fit engine. Its REST state is no longer uniform: it is a specimen ramp across the seven letters, from 4 at wdth 50 / wght 100 rising to R at wdth 150 / wght 900, so the still frame already says 'whisper -> LOUD'. Under each letter: a hairline tick and a 10px mono readout 'W 050 · G 100' that updates live (tabular figures, 30 Hz). Lower rule: tagline 'I build interfaces that move.' on the left ('move.' in IKB italic, wdth 120 / wght 800), the availability ping in the centre, 'SCROLL TO TURN IT UP ↓' on the right. A fixed WebGL pigment layer (difference blend) sits over the hero. INTERACTION: the v1 proximity lens now modulates around the ramp. Horizontal pointer velocity shears each letter (skewX ≤12°, spring k 170 / c 13), so a fast swipe makes the word wobble like jelly. The pointer paints IKB pigment: paper under it turns Klein blue, ink letters it crosses turn monogold, and it dries in ~2.5 s. Click or tap a letter for a 'strike': it punches to 150/900, springs back with overshoot, throws a radial pigment burst and plays a tick. After 2.6 s idle, the v1 auto-lens 'breathes'; after 8.6 s it returns to the rest ramp. INTRO: 'Calibration' (move 2) runs in place. The hero assembles itself out of the font-loading state, with no curtain and no content hidden behind an opacity gate. PHONE (390x844): the name splits into 4BOO / SER, each line width-fitted, and the ramp continues across the lines (light at the top left, black at the bottom right). Readouts are 9px. The hero fills 100svh with the tagline and availability under the name. Every active touch is both a brush and a lens, so two fingers make two lenses. Horizontal drags paint and morph, and vertical scrolling still paints a stroke along the thumb's path (passive touchmove keeps firing during native scroll). After the intro, a 'ghost fingertip' (a 24px IKB ring) sweeps once across the name, painting a stroke beside a 'DRAG ACROSS THE NAME' chip that disappears on the first touch. REDUCED MOTION: static ramp, static readouts, no pigment, no intro.

moves.name: Rewind: curtain call
moves.section: Foot bar at the very end -> back to the hero
moves.experience: The last control on the page is a full-width mono bar, 'REWIND ↑ PLAY IT AGAIN', replacing 'Back to top'. On click, the footer's physics letters get an upward kick and fly out of the band. The page then auto-scrolls to the top in 2.4 s, and every scroll-driven system plays backwards at full speed for free: the flood flaps un-flip in a rolling clatter, the board flips back MOTION -> STRATEGY, the O shrinks back out of the ink, work rows flash their blue wipe as they pass the centre, the tapes ring at full amplitude, and the VOL meter counts 100 -> 000. On arrival the hero replays a 0.9 s short Calibration (axis reels plus ghost stroke). The site ends where it began: a loop.
moves.implementation: lenis.scrollTo(0, {duration: 2.4, easing: easeInOutQuart, lock: true, onComplete: () => intro({short: true})}). A global 'rewinding' flag gives rows that cross the viewport centre a 120 ms is-on flash, throttled to one per 120 ms. Physics: Body.applyForce upward on all letters, plus world gravity.y = -1 for 400 ms. Sound: a whoosh, plus each system's own clatter as it is scrubbed. When it finishes, focus moves to the h1 (tabindex -1).
moves.phone: window.scrollTo({top: 0, behavior: 'smooth'}) (native smooth scroll on iOS and Android). Detect arrival with 'scrollend' (or a scrollY < 2 poll) to fire the short intro. vibrate([10,40,10]) when instrument mode is on.
moves.perf_and_fallback: Nothing new to render: it is the existing scroll path at high speed. Reduced motion: instant jump to the top and focus the h1. If Lenis is missing, use native smooth scroll.

moves.name: Calibration: the hero builds itself
moves.section: Intro -> hero (time-based, 0-2.7 s)
moves.experience: No loading curtain. 0-450 ms: the spec rule draws left to right as a wdth ruler (ticks 50...150 in 9px mono), and a mono line 'ANYBODY VF · WDTH 50-150 · WGHT 100-900 - 000%' counts the real font load. 200-1500 ms: the seven letters appear as hairlines and run like slot-machine reels through widths and weights. Each axis jumps in discrete steps that slow down (40 -> 160 ms per step). The line stays width-fitted, so the letters jostle for space while the readouts under them spin like odometers. The reels lock left to right, 110 ms apart, each landing on its ramp value with a small spring overshoot. 1500-1900 ms: the ruler ticks fade into the four spec labels, which decode-scramble in; tagline words rise; the availability dot pings. 1900-2700 ms: a ghost brush sweeps an S-curve across the name, laying the first IKB stroke while the letters bulge as it passes, then hands control to the visitor. At 2300 ms the tapes snap taut.
moves.implementation: Extend the v1 Kinetic class with mode 'intro': tgt[i] comes from a per-letter step schedule (step interval 40·1.32^k ms, each value random and different from the previous one, final value = the ramp value). Writes snap (k = 1) during steps; the lock uses a critically damped spring (k 220, c 18). Readouts: one child span per .k, text written every second frame. Font: document.fonts.load('400 100px Anybody'); a fake ramp to 90% over 1.2 s, jump to 100 on resolve. After a 3.5 s timeout, skip the reels and use the fallback face. Decode: each character cycles through A-Z0-9 for 180 ms, staggered left to right by 12 ms. Ghost: a cubic Bézier from (-0.1W, nameY+0.2H) to (1.1W, nameY-0.1H), easeInOutCubic over 800 ms, which feeds P.x/P.y (kind 'ghost') and fluid.splat(dx, dy). Any wheel, key, pointerdown or touch fast-forwards to the lock in 250 ms. A sessionStorage flag (inside try/catch) gives repeat visits a 0.9 s version.
moves.phone: Same sequence, in place, on the two-line name. The ghost becomes a visible 24px IKB fingertip ring with a 'DRAG ACROSS THE NAME' chip, which teaches the gesture where there is no hover. 2.4 s in total.
moves.perf_and_fallback: Only font-variation writes on 7 spans. If WebGL pigment is unavailable, the ghost still sweeps the type lens (without paint). Reduced motion: no intro; the hero renders at rest at once. Content is always in the DOM and readable, with no opacity-0 gate.

moves.name: Crop-mark cursor and tap echo
moves.section: Global (every section)
moves.experience: The cursor is a layout-app selection tool. By default: a 6px dot inside four L-shaped crop marks (an 18x18 box) that trail with a slight elastic lag. Over hero or footer letters, the marks wrap the nearest glyph and a chip shows its live axes, 'W 132 · G 812': the page is being inspected. Over links and buttons, the marks spring out to the element's bounds (+6px) with an action chip (OPEN, COPY, ↗ GITHUB, SOUND ON), and the element leans up to 6px toward the pointer. Over a work row they frame the title with 'VIEW CASE 02'. Over a footer letter they show 'GRAB'; while dragging, 'THROW' plus a 1px vector line for fling direction and speed. Keyboard focus uses the same marks, so the focus ring IS the cursor.
moves.implementation: A fixed rig: 4 corner divs (10px arms, 1.5px borders on two sides), a dot and a chip. mix-blend-mode: difference over paper and ink; plain paper over blue zones (v1 zone logic). State comes from pointerover delegation reading data-cursor / data-cursor-label. Only the active target's rect is re-read, once per frame. Each corner springs toward its target corner (k .25 per frame, dt-normalised); the dot lerps at .35. The magnet is a transform on an inner span of the target, so layout never changes. focusin plus :focus-visible moves the rig to the focused element, and those elements' outlines are hidden. The native cursor stays for text inputs.
moves.phone: No cursor. 'Tap echo': on tapping any interactive element, the crop marks flash around it and snap shut in 280 ms (plus a 6 ms haptic in instrument mode). Same visual language, used as touch feedback.
moves.perf_and_fallback: 5 transformed elements and 1 rect read per frame. Reduced motion: the marks snap without springs and there is no magnet. Coarse pointers: the rig is not rendered.

moves.name: Instrument mode: synthesized sound and haptics
moves.section: Global: nav toggle, then every event on the page
moves.experience: A 'SOUND ○ OFF' toggle in the nav. Switching it on plays a 3-note boot chirp, and the page becomes a quiet instrument: ticks on hover and focus, mechanical clatter from every split-flap, a plucked note when the tapes ring (pitch from where you pluck), soft thuds panned left and right as footer letters land, an airy whoosh on case open and at the bottom of the O zoom, and a two-note ding on copy. Crescendo: the master low-pass opens from 1.6 to 7.6 kHz and gain rises .5 -> .8 with scroll progress, so the page literally gets louder on the way down to 'LOUD'. The nav VU meter (10 bars, VOL 000-100) shows progress, with peak-hold kicks on fast scrolls.
moves.implementation: A lazy AudioContext, created on the toggle click (a user gesture). Graph: voices -> master lowpass BiquadFilter -> DynamicsCompressor -> Gain -> destination. tick: a 3 ms white-noise buffer -> highpass 4 kHz, gain .05. flap: 6-9 ms of noise -> bandpass 1.8-2.6 kHz (random Q 2-4), gain .06-.1; at most 12 voices; scheduled on AudioContext time (the flood schedules its clicks ahead, max 40/s). pluck: Karplus-Strong rendered in JS into 5 AudioBuffers per tape (A minor pentatonic A2 C3 D3 E3 G3, tape B an octave higher; 1.2 s each, feedback .996, two-tap averaging lowpass), picked by pluck x. thud: sine 90 -> 42 Hz exponential ramp over 140 ms plus 30 ms of low-passed noise; gain ∝ impact speed from Matter collisionStart; StereoPannerNode by x; one per body per 30 ms. whoosh: noise -> bandpass sweep 400 -> 2400 Hz over 500 ms. Suspend when the tab is hidden. The preference is kept in localStorage (inside try/catch); on return the toggle reads 'SOUND ON - TAP TO RESUME'. VU ballistics: 30 ms attack, 600 ms release on |velocity|.
moves.phone: A compact '♪ OFF' in the phone nav. Instrument mode also turns on haptics where they exist (navigator.vibrate on Android): tick 6 ms, flap batch 4 ms, project change 10 ms, grab 8 ms, impact min(25, 2v) ms, copy [8,30,8]. iOS has no Vibration API, so haptics are skipped there; the iOS 18 checkbox 'switch' haptic trick is an optional experiment, off by default.
moves.perf_and_fallback: Nodes are created per event and garbage-collected. No audio files; a one-time ~5 ms Karplus-Strong synthesis. Off by default, and nothing is created until the visitor opts in. Sound never autoplays.

moves.name: The O threshold
moves.section: New pinned threshold between Work (paper) and Process (ink), 160svh
moves.experience: After the last project, the services heading arrives on paper: a hairline 'HOW A PROJECT' over a fat 'MOVES' (wdth 150 / wght 900). It holds for a beat of reading (the first 30% of the pin). Then scrolling pulls you into the O. It scales from 1x to ~70x around a point inside its thick left stroke, accelerating (p³) like a fall, while the other letters are sucked thin (wdth -> 50) and drift outward. The screen goes fully ink (you are inside the letter), and the board's labels decode in on black. Scroll back up and you climb out of the O. The colour change is made of type, not a background edge.
moves.implementation: Section height 160svh; inner sticky 100svh on paper. At layout, measure the O span; transform-origin = (0.14·width, 0.5·height) in its own box. Per frame: q = smoothstep(.3, .9, p); s = 1 + 69·q³; transform: scale(s). Do NOT set will-change, so the browser re-rasterises the single glyph crisply each frame. Siblings: wdth lerps toward 50, translateX(±q·20vw), opacity 1 - q. An ink overlay inside the sticky has opacity = smoothstep(12, 20, s); after s > 20 the glyph stops scaling and holds, so no giant raster is ever painted. Whoosh at s ≈ 8 in instrument mode. The real h2 stays in the DOM for screen readers.
moves.phone: Same behaviour. MOVES is fitted to 390px, and the pin shrinks to 140svh so one thumb flick carries you through. It is scrubbed, so it follows the finger and native momentum exactly.
moves.perf_and_fallback: One glyph repaint per frame while s < 20 (~1-2 ms), then a single opacity layer. Reduced motion or no JS: no pin; the heading sits static on paper with a hard cut to ink (the v1 behaviour).

moves.name: Jog-wheel index (phone work)
moves.section: Work, ≤760px
moves.experience: On phones the index becomes a machine you feed with your thumb. A sticky 'monitor' (44svh, ink, full width inside the gutters) pins under the nav. It shows ONE live project artwork, with a mono overlay '02 / 05 - PULSE RECORDS · 2025' and a 5-segment index bar. The big titles scroll up beneath it, and whichever title crosses the focus line (monitor bottom + 18svh) becomes active: blue wipe from the direction you came from, the title widens from wdth 62 to 112, the monitor swaps its artwork with a fast horizontal wipe, the counter flaps and a haptic ticks. Flick hard and the monitor flickers through the projects like a slot machine, then settles. Tap the active row for the title flight into its case.
moves.implementation: Rows min-height 24svh. The active index comes from cached row offsetTops vs scrollY (no per-frame rect reads), with 6svh hysteresis. The monitor is one canvas (or the shared WebGL preview from the visuals lens) that draws only the active artwork. Swap: render the new artwork into a second canvas, then clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0) -> inset(0) over 380 ms. When |v| > 25 px/frame, swaps are instant and throttled to one per 90 ms.
moves.phone: This IS the phone design. Desktop keeps the hover list with the cursor-side preview, framed by the crop marks.
moves.perf_and_fallback: Cheaper than v1: one animated canvas instead of up to five inline ones. Reduced motion: no sticky monitor; each row gets inline static artwork, as in v1.

moves.name: Process board + the flood to IKB
moves.section: Services / Process (ink, pinned) and its exit into the blue band
moves.experience: Pinned on ink, a Solari departure board spans the width: 8 big split-flap tiles with dark #18181C faces, a hairline hinge across the middle and paper glyphs. Scrolling moves through four stages. Each stage change triggers a ~0.5 s cascade in which every tile flips through 2-5 random letters before landing, left to right, on STRATEGY -> DESIGN -> DEVELOP -> MOTION. The type gets heavier at each stage (wght 250 -> 450 -> 650 -> 900 italic), so the process is itself a crescendo. Under the board, the stage copy and deliverables swap with a decode scramble, and a mono bar reads 'STAGE 02 / 04' over a 4-tick rail. Scrolling has detents: stop between stages and it clicks to the nearest one. The final 70svh is THE FLOOD: the 8 tiles flip to blank IKB faces, then a diagonal wave of small flaps crosses the whole viewport and turns black into Klein blue with a rolling clatter. The pin releases into the blue band with no seam.
moves.implementation: Section height 100svh + 4x60svh + 70svh; inner sticky 100svh. The stage index comes from progress with 4% hysteresis. Each tile has 4 leaves: static top (next glyph), static bottom (current glyph), flipping top (current, rotateX 0 -> -90°), flipping bottom (next, rotateX 90° -> 0). Each leaf shows half a glyph (overflow hidden plus a line-height offset), with perspective 900px, hidden backfaces, and a shading pseudo-element whose opacity follows the angle. Sequence per tile: current + n random letters (n = 2 + (3i mod 4)) + target. Each flap takes 70 ms (the first 90 ms); tile i starts after 30·i ms. Scrolling back runs the same sequence toward the previous word. Short words are centred, with blank tiles around them. The copy swap is a 240 ms decode. All four stages also exist as a visually hidden list, and the board itself is aria-hidden. Detents: when |lenis.velocity| < .1 for 160 ms inside the board and the scroll position is more than 8svh from a stage centre, lenis.scrollTo(centre, {duration: .7, easing: easeOutCubic}). Flood: one 2D canvas (DPR ≤1.5) over the sticky, as a 16x10 grid. Each cell's angle θ = 180°·smoothstep(0, 1, (p - d)/.25), with d = (i+j)/(cols+rows)·.75. Draw the ink leaf scaled by cos θ until 90°, then the IKB leaf, darkening near 90°. A flap click is scheduled whenever a cell crosses 90° (at most 40/s). At p = 1 the canvas is solid #1D2CF3, the same colour as the band.
moves.phone: The board becomes 2 rows x 4 tiles (~84x112px) reading STRA/TEGY, DESI/GN, DEVE/LOP, MOTI/ON; real Solari boards wrap like that. The copy sits under the board. Detents use CSS scroll-snap-type: y proximity on html, with four invisible snap markers that exist only inside the board. Flood grid 6x12. A 4 ms haptic per flap batch in instrument mode.
moves.perf_and_fallback: 32 transformed leaves during ~0.5 s bursts. The flood draws at most 160 rects per frame, and only during its 70svh. Reduced motion or no JS: no pin; the four stages render as a static stacked list (v1 phone styling), and the flood is replaced by a static row of IKB flap tiles along the band's top edge.

moves.name: Title flight + gesture case sheet
moves.section: Work rows -> case sheet overlay
moves.experience: Click a row (tap on phones) and the title physically travels. The blue sheet still grows out of the row band (the v1 clip-path), while each letter of 'PULSE RECORDS' flies from the row to its place in the giant case header. The letters leave left to right in a stagger, widening and thickening in flight (wdth 62 -> 150, wght 700 -> 900), so the row name becomes the case cover. Closing reverses it: the letters fly home and the row wipes back to paper. 'Next case' flips the title letters, split-flap style, to the next project's name, and the counter '(CASE 03 / 05)' flips with it.
moves.implementation: Row titles are pre-split into letter spans. Open: read the First rects (row letters). Fill the case and run the existing fitCaseTitle measure pass to get the Last rects at the final axes and font size; hide the real case letters (opacity 0). Create a fixed 'flight' layer of clones at the First positions (font size, axes, paper colour). For 820 ms (ease .76,0,.24,1; delay 14·i ms), translate each clone between its rects and interpolate font-size and font-variation-settings. At the end, show the real letters and remove the clones in the same frame. Closing mirrors First and Last. The clip-path sheet and the rising content work as in v1 (content delay 600 ms). Call lenis.stop() while the sheet is open, and put data-lenis-prevent on .case-scroll. In instrument mode: whoosh on open, flap clatter on next.
moves.phone: Swipe down on the sheet when its scroller is at the top: the sheet follows the finger (translateY, with rubber-banding past 40% of its height), while the title letters lag behind on per-letter springs, like jelly. Release past 120px, or faster than 0.6 px/ms, closes it with the reverse flight; otherwise it springs back (k 300, c 26). A horizontal swipe (|dx| > 60 and |dx| > 1.5·|dy|) goes to the next or previous case with the flap. 10 ms haptic on close and next.
moves.perf_and_fallback: At most 13 absolutely positioned clones for 0.8 s; font-size changes affect only the fixed layer. Reduced motion: v1's instant open and close, no flight, plain text swap for next.

moves.name: Make ___ LOUD: physics finale
moves.section: Footer band (blue): headline + playground + CTA
moves.experience: The headline LET'S MAKE / SOMETHING / LOUD. hangs over three hairline shelves. When the band reaches 30% of the viewport, the shelves draw and the letters drop onto them one by one with thuds, squashing on impact (wdth +25, wght +150, then springing back). Once settled, it reads perfectly. Grab any letter and throw it: fast letters stretch wide and heavy, and knocked letters tumble into a pile on the floor. Below is 'MAKE ___ LOUD' with chips (YOUR BRAND / MY APP / OUR LAUNCH) and a free input. On submit, SOMETHING is kicked off its shelf, and the visitor's word falls from above the band onto the empty shelf, landing upright in place: 'LET'S MAKE NOCTURNE LOUD.' The email CTA becomes 'Tell me about NOCTURNE →' with the subject prefilled. Leave it alone for 9 s, or press RESET TYPE, and every letter springs home in a cascade: Swiss order restores itself.
moves.implementation: matter-js 0.19.0 (pinned, jsdelivr or cdnjs). The world is the headline box in band coordinates: walls at its sides, the floor at its bottom (the contact block below is untouched DOM). Bodies are rectangles from each glyph's ink box, measured once from the fitted DOM, and rendered as aria-hidden absolutely positioned spans moved with translate/rotate, so they keep the real font and live axes. Shelves are static thin rects at each baseline. Drop: bodies are created 0.25em above home and released 28 ms apart (left to right, line by line); gravity 1.4, restitution .25, friction .6, sleeping on. Squash: on collisionStart, add an axis-spring impulse ∝ relative speed. Drag: a custom pointer constraint (Query.point hit test -> Constraint with stiffness .2, damping .1); while moving, wdth = 100 + min(50, 4·speed). Word swap: sanitise to [A-Z0-9 &!?.-], max 12 characters; fit the size to the line. Kick the old letters with applyForce up and sideways, and make shelf 2 a sensor for 600 ms. Spawn the new bodies above their target x with inertia Infinity so they land upright, and restore inertia once they sleep. Re-typeset: turn collisions off and tween position and angle home over 650 ms (easeOutBack, 18 ms stagger); evicted floor letters fade out. The h2 keeps real sr-only text, updated through an aria-live polite region. The engine steps from the shared rAF with a fixed 1/60 accumulator (max 2 substeps), and only while the band is on screen.
moves.phone: Fingers grab letters directly. A non-passive touchstart/touchmove pair calls preventDefault only when the touch started on a letter body, so dragging on empty blue still scrolls. Flick to throw. The chips mean no keyboard is needed; the input is still there, with visualViewport handling the keyboard. An optional TILT chip appears only if DeviceOrientation events actually arrive (iOS needs requestPermission from the tap, and the artifact iframe may block it; if so, the chip stays hidden). Tilt maps gravity to (sin γ, sin β), and a hard shake (devicemotion > 18 m/s²) scatters the letters. One haptic per impact in instrument mode.
moves.perf_and_fallback: At most 40 bodies, sleeping, paused when off screen: under 1 ms per frame. Reduced motion: no physics and no drop; the headline is static, and the word swap replaces the text instantly and still updates the mailto. If the CDN fails: the same static path.

moves.name: Plucked tapes
moves.section: Skills tapes under the hero
moves.experience: The two crossing tapes are strung across the page like strings, sagging slightly at rest. Scroll hard and they ring with a damped standing wave; the words ride the curve and tilt with it, then settle when you stop. Sweep the pointer across a tape to pluck it at that spot, and a bump runs along it. With sound on, each pluck plays a pentatonic note chosen by where you plucked. The tapes cross at only one point, so no words are hidden.
moves.implementation: Each tape is a 1D wave equation on N = 64 nodes with fixed ends (Verlet, 2 substeps per frame, ~1.2 Hz fundamental, damping .985). Scroll acceleration adds force on mode 1 (sin πx). A pluck is a Gaussian displacement (σ = 4 nodes) wherever the pointer crosses the tape line at speed. The ribbon is one SVG path (2xN points) updated each frame. Glyphs are spans placed at arc length s (marquee offset + cached advances, measured once with offsetWidth); y is interpolated from the nodes, with rotate(atan(slope)) and translate3d. Only visible glyphs are updated.
moves.phone: A horizontal thumb swipe grabs a tape like a DJ platter: the text scrubs 1:1 with the finger, and on release it keeps the fling velocity and decays back to base speed. A tap plucks. Vertical drags still scroll (touch-action: pan-y). N = 40 nodes.
moves.perf_and_fallback: About 100 transform writes and 2 path updates per frame while visible (gated by IntersectionObserver). Reduced motion: two straight, static tapes with all the text visible. No JS: the v1 CSS tapes.

moves.name: Living brush: Klein pigment
moves.section: Paper zone above Work (hero, tapes, manifesto)
moves.experience: Your pointer is a Klein 'living brush'. It lays down pigment that swirls and bleeds like wet paint: paper under it becomes International Klein Blue, and ink letters it crosses become monogold, so the text inverts instead of disappearing. The paint sticks to the paper as you scroll and dries away in ~2.5 s, so the page is always readable at rest. It is staged, not wallpaper: the intro ghost paints the first stroke, a letter strike throws a radial burst, and when the reader reaches the end of the manifesto the ghost underlines 'move,' with one IKB stroke.
moves.implementation: One WebGL canvas (WebGL2, falling back to WebGL1 + OES_texture_half_float with linear filtering), fixed and full-viewport. Backing store at 0.5x (phone) / 0.75x (desktop) of CSS size; pointer-events none; mix-blend-mode: difference; below the nav and cursor. Stable-fluid solver (Stam / Dobryakov style): sim grid 128 (phone) / 192 (desktop) on the short side, dye 512 / 768, Jacobi 8 / 16 iterations, vorticity 18, dye half-life ~0.9 s. Scroll advection: the advect shader samples at uv + vec2(0, Δscroll/viewportH), so paint moves with the page. Display output, premultiplied: X·d with alpha d, where X = #C9BB00. That gives |paper - X| ≈ #1D2CE3 (IKB) and |ink - X| ≈ #BBAD10 (gold). Zone mask: d is multiplied by a 40px vertical feather that ends at the Work section's viewport top; this keeps pigment off ink and blue zones, where IKB would turn lavender. Splat sources: pointer deltas; every active touch, including passive touchmove during native scroll; ghost paths; strike bursts. The sim pauses when the zone is off screen or when there has been no splat for 3 s (the dye is surely gone): clear the canvas and stop GPU work.
moves.phone: Every active touch is a brush: several fingers paint at once on taps, holds and horizontal drags, and pinch-zoom still works. Scrolling with the thumb leaves a stroke along its path. 0.5x backing store, 128 grid, 8 iterations.
moves.perf_and_fallback: About 1.5-2.5 ms of GPU time on an integrated laptop GPU, plus one full-screen difference-blend layer to composite; measure this in Safari. Fallback when float textures are missing, or by a low-power heuristic (coarse pointer + hardwareConcurrency ≤ 4 + under 45 fps for 1 s): a CSS 'dab' mode of radial-gradient blobs with difference blend that grow and fade over 1.2 s. Reduced motion: off entirely. While running, the sim never overlaps the Work preview WebGL (the zones exclude each other).

page_sequence: B0 CALIBRATION (intro, time-based, 0-2.7 s; 0.9 s on repeat visits; any input fast-forwards in 250 ms): the spec rule + wdth ruler draws (0-450 ms) -> letters reel through the axes and lock left to right (200-1500 ms) -> labels decode, tagline rises (1500-1900 ms) -> the ghost brush paints the first IKB stroke (1900-2700 ms) -> tapes snap taut (2300 ms).

B1 SPECIMEN (hero, 100svh): the name rests on the hairline -> black ramp with live W/G readouts. Proximity lens, velocity shear, pigment brush, letter strike. Idle 2.6 s -> auto-breath; 8.6 s -> rest. Phone: multi-touch brushes and lenses; the ghost fingertip teaches the gesture.
B2 STRINGS (tapes, ~70vh): two plucked-string marquees crossing at one point. They ring with scroll speed, hover plucks them, and on phones a thumb scrubs them like a platter.

B3 READ (manifesto + stats, ~130vh): the calm beat, the only one without a toy. Words ink in by weight and colour (wght 300 mute #5C5F69 -> 520 ink, readable either way) as they cross a reading line at 62% of the viewport. At 85% the ghost brush underlines 'move,' in IKB. The stats 6+ / 40+ / 12 split-flap in (600 ms, 120 ms stagger), foreshadowing the board.

B4 INDEX (work; desktop ~100vh, phone 44svh monitor + 5x24svh rows): desktop has the hover wipe from the entry edge, a cursor-side preview and crop marks 'VIEW CASE 0n'; phones have the jog wheel with haptic ticks. Click or tap -> TITLE FLIGHT (820 ms) into the case sheet overlay (phone: swipe down to dismiss, left/right for next/prev with a flapping title; desktop: Esc, ←/→).

B5 THRESHOLD (160svh pinned, paper -> ink): 0-30% hold on 'HOW A PROJECT MOVES'; 30-90% zoom into the O's stroke (1x -> 70x, p³), other letters sucked thin; 90-100% full ink, board labels decode. Fully reversible.

B6 BOARD (pinned, 100svh + 4x60svh, ink): STRATEGY wght 250 -> DESIGN 450 -> DEVELOP 650 -> MOTION 900 italic. Each change is a ~0.5 s flap cascade with a decoded copy swap. Detents snap to stage centres (Lenis 0.7 s on desktop; CSS snap proximity on phones).

B7 FLOOD (last 70svh of the board, scrubbed): the tiles flip to blank IKB, then a diagonal wave of 16x10 flaps (6x12 on phones) turns the whole screen from ink to Klein blue with a rolling clatter. The pin releases into the identical blue band with no seam.

B8 LOUD (band, ~100svh): when the band's top reaches 30% of the viewport, the shelves draw (380 ms) and the letters drop onto them 28 ms apart with thuds and axis squash (~1.1 s total). 'MAKE ___ LOUD' playground (chips plus input): SOMETHING is kicked to the floor and the visitor's word falls onto the shelf. Letters can be thrown; auto re-typeset after 9 s idle; the mailto subject becomes 'Let's make [WORD] loud'.
B9 CONTACT (in the band, ~60svh): the email at display size with crop marks 'COPY'. Copying triggers a wdth ripple left to right (400 ms), a ding and a toast. Links, the flapping clock, location.
B10 CURTAIN CALL (2.4 s): REWIND ↑ -> the letters fly out of the band, the page rushes back through every beat in reverse, and arrival replays the 0.9 s calibration. The loop closes.
